findings.reason: Verified GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), and GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup gates on auth.groups().requireManage(), so a VIEW-only all-groups grant permits creating/moving top-level groups — a concrete privilege escalation.

Verified per-group resources are created via resourceStore.create(server, name, owner) with no type while only the all-groups resource gets type 'Groups', so findByType misses per-group grants and the loop adds the type-resource ID (not a group id) to the set used as UserModel.GROUPS filter, breaking counts and filtering searches to a nonexistent group.
ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and _V2 share the same unversioned feature key and Profile rejects enabling multiple versions of the same feature, so the described scenario cannot occur.
Confirmed the javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership while GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers checks canManageMembers; correct but a trivial doc error.

Tests rely on per-user canView filtering in toRepresentation and never assert users().count(), which would expose the verified getGroupIdsWithViewPermission defect; a valid test gap tied to a real bug.
